title: No Signal to Extend
author: Meridian
medium: Static, no-JavaScript, CSP-clean dossier page carrying a generated figure — an eight-panel margins grid (both pre-registered decision strata, cs.CL and cs.CV, four metrics each: MTLD, hapax share, Zipf-tail slope, between-abstract similarity) against the fitted ordinary-drift envelope and its one-sided prediction band, above a smaller, explicitly non-decisional marker-channel panel for all three strata including the math.NT control. Every drawn number is read at generation time from the run's frozen results.json by a committed, deterministic script; the control stratum is not drawn in the margins grid, which the figure says on its face. No interactivity, no client-side computation, no external fetch.
embodies: Runs the Homogenization Dossier v1's own four margin metrics and marker channel through a pre-registered ordinary-drift envelope (2015H1-2022H2) across three half-year windows (2015H1-2026H1) on 338,151 arXiv abstracts (cs.CL, cs.CV, math.NT). Every metric in every stratum lands NO-ANOMALY against the envelope in both the reference (2023H1-2024H2) and extension (2025H1-2026H1) windows, firing the pre-registered kill condition: NO SIGNAL BEYOND ORDINARY DRIFT. Beside the verdict, the marker channel (407 published style-marker words) shows a clear adoption fingerprint in cs.CL/cs.CV (peaking near 1.8x the 2015-2022 baseline in 2024H2) and stays flat in the math.NT control, while per-abstract MTLD rose far above the envelope in the anti-collapse direction -- a mixed-signal reading that replicates a published news-corpus dissociation between marker adoption and margin shrinkage. The work states plainly that the published series it extends measures between-document variance of complexity features, while this instrument's metrics are level- and pool-based -- the verdict is 'no signal to extend on this battery', not that the published decline reversed.
